3 The present Review Petition is filed seeking review of the order of this Court passed in W.P.No.4973 of 2015 dated 04.08.2023.
2.

The claim of the petitioners in the present review petition is that this Court directed the respondents either to pay the compensation on par with other 14 assignees or to handover the demarcated physical possession of the land admeasuring to an extent of Ac.1.50 cents each to the petitioners in survey No.351/IP.
Learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that the present review petition is filed seeking for compensation.
He further submits that the compensation which was paid to the other 14 assignees is on 09.09.2014, but the same was not yet awarded to the petitioners.

Since all these years, the petitioners are suffering with livelihood and as such the compensation should be paid as per the market value of the property as on today in terms of the Right to Fair Compensation and and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013).

entities.text: Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation Resettlement Act, 2013 (Act 30 of 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He further submits that earlier the compensation in respect of the assigned lands was paid dated to the other assignees on the basis of G.O.Ms.No.512, 27.09.2013.
He further submits that after enactment of Act 30 of 2013, the G.O., issued basing upon the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 cannot be enforced.
As such the petitioner is entitled for compensation at the rate of present market value and in terms of Act 30 of 2013.

3. For which, learned counsel for the 4*^ respondent filed counter-affidavit, wherein it is stated that the Revenue Divisional Officer, Gudur resumed an extent of Ac.31.84 cents in survey Nos.362/1,
363/1 and 363/2 etc., of Chittedu Village and paid the exgratia to the 18 eligible beneficiaries vide proceedings in Rc.A2.1219/2012, dated 09.09.2014.
The compensation for the land situated in survey No.351/IP of Chittedu Village is not paid, as the said land is not resumed by the Government.
An extent of Ac. 1.50 cents each in survey No.351/IP of Chittedu Village, Kota Mandal, Tirupathi District was assigned to the petitioners under Darakasth Rules.
The land is not taken from the petitioners for the public purpose till today and also the said land is not required to the Government as on today.
If, the said land is required to the Government, the authorities may resume the land from them by following due procedure and by paying the exgratia/compensation to the petitioners.
But, the land is not taken from the petitioners for public purpose, hence, the allotment of alternative land or for payment of compensation does not arise.
A 4. Learned Government Pleader for the respondents further admitted that all the petitioners were assigned the land admeasuring to an extent of Ac.1.50 cents each in survey No.351/1P.
Since, the subject land was not acquired by the respondents, they need not be Still the paid any compensation in favour of the petitioners.
petitioners are having possession of their land.
Therefore, they are not entitled for any relief as claimed in the Review Petition.
5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Government Pleader for the respondents.

sentences.text: The subject review petition is only seeking clarification with regard to the compensation which was directed to be payable by the respondents on par with 14 assignees.

In view of the enactment of Act 30 of 2013, the compensation paid to the 14 assignees on 09.09.2014 may not be applicable,
since, the basis for payment of compensation on 09.09.2014 is not available after enactment of Act V. 30 of 2013.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as per the terms of Act 30 of 2013.
Therefore, the review petitioners herein rightly pleaded for modification of the orders of this Court dated 04.08.2023.

The other contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that even though the respondents are reiterating their contention that the subject land of the petitioners was not acquired for the purpose of subject project, but this Court disbelieved the contention of the respondents and directed to pay the compensation or to handover the land assigned to the petitioners, since they categorically admitted that the assignment of the subject lands in favour of the petitioners and the said fact was also reiterated in the counter-affidavit filed in this review petition.

The contention of the learned Government Pleader that the subject land of the petitioners was situated in survey No.351/IP, the land situated in survey No.351/IP was not at all acquired by the respondents for the public purpose, so they need not be paid any compensation to be considered subject to delivery of the possession of the property to the petitioners which was assigned to the petitioners.

It is further observed that mere stating a fact that the subject land of the petitioners was neither acquired nor required, the respondents should able to demarcate the land of the petitioners which was assigned in their favour from the acquired land in survey No.351/IP, Tr--" '72 % having admitted the assignment and same is situated in survey N0.351/1P.
8.

In view of the reasons stated above, the respondents are hereby directed to demarcate the subject land assigned to the petitioners in survey No.351/1P or 351 within a period of three months from the date of receipt of copy of this Order or otherwise, if the respondents are unable to demarcate the property of the petitioners, the respondents are directed to initiate acquisition proceedings as per the terms of Act 30 of 2013 within a period of three months thereafter.
9. With the above direction, the Review Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel miscellaneous application, pending, if any, shall also stand closed.
Sd/- N. NAGAMM
